label: Equal Vision Records
lede: Vic DiCara played guitar beside Zack de la Rocha in Inside Out, then built 108 out of Vedic scripture. The band toured in a school bus turned temple, fought anti-Krishna flyer crews, and broke up in 1996 when DiCara left for India to live as a monk. It came back in 2005, minus the temple.

eras.title: Out of Inside Out
eras.text: Vic DiCara had played bass in Beyond, guitar beside Zack de la Rocha in Inside Out, and guitar for Ray Cappo in Shelter. In 1991 he started 108 in New York and put Krishna consciousness into every song, where the Cro-Mags and Antidote had only hinted at it.

years.cap: Vic DiCara on guitar with Inside Out
years.src: Wikipedia: 108 (band) · The Vinyl Factory · Punknews · Anti-Matter
years.h: Vic DiCara starts 108 and takes the name from a string of prayer beads
years.p: He has just left Inside Out, where Zack de la Rocha sang, and Shelter. The Hare Krishna devotee (Vraja Kishor das) names the band for the 108 beads on a japa mala, and a self-released demo follows the same year.
years.xp:
The Vinyl Factory's history of Krishnacore says DiCara had written the title song of Inside Out's only record as a Krishna-conscious anthem before he started 108. He told Anti-Matter that back then "I was oblivious to ISKCON," and that leaving Inside Out for a partnership with Ray Cappo was "a dumb move, from an artistic standpoint."

With 108 he went further: the lyrics leaned so hard on Vedic texts that the first album came with a glossary. "This 108 thing is my bhajan," he told Anti-Matter. "It's not my preaching; it's an expression." Punknews later reported he was a temple president in New Jersey while playing in 108 and translating Sanskrit scripture on the side.

eras.title: A temple on wheels
eras.text: With Rob Fish committed and Equal Vision Records behind them, 108 spent most of 1993 on the road with Shelter in a bus that doubled as a temple. Their drummer later called them a very militant band, and there were brawls to back it up.

years.src: No Echo: Rob Fish · Discogs · The Vinyl Factory
years.h: Equal Vision releases Holyname, and the CD plays as one track
years.p: The liner notes carry a glossary for the Vedic terms, and a pressing error ran the whole disc as a single 43-minute track, per Discogs.
years.xp:
Discogs credits list sessions at The Station in Maryland, going back to December 1991. Fish told No Echo he was in the studio for maybe two hours: "I was in the studio for maybe 2 hours and everything was already recorded." A drummer named Zach, from Worlds Collide, played on it, and DiCara played everything else.

The Vinyl Factory's Colin Helb calls the record heavy, intense and powerful.

years.h: Rob Fish's first 108 show is in Reading, Pennsylvania, with Shelter
years.p: He skipped 108's first tour date in September 1992, and the Ressurection singer (Rasaraja dasa) recommitted in January 1993. His first show is March 15, at Unisound.
years.xp:
Fish told No Echo that Vic DiCara called him the day after 108's first show, in Atlantic City, where Ressurection also played. Fish hesitated because he felt he didn't fit in philosophically, and simply didn't turn up for the September 1992 date.

The two talked it through in January 1993. "I liked the idea of playing with Vraja, because he was an awesome guitar player," Fish said. The run with Shelter lasted five months.

years.src: The Guardian · No Echo: Chris Daly
years.h: A retired school bus becomes 108's temple, and Chris Daly its drummer
years.p: Equal Vision's Steve Reddy recruits Daly in spring 1993, and he heads out with Shelter on a converted school bus that doubles as a traveling temple.
years.xp:
Daly told The Guardian: "That tour was a travelling Krishna fest", with cooking and setting up in parking lots, about the closest hardcore came to being a Deadhead.

He hid the band's Krishna outlook from his Roman Catholic parents, he told No Echo, telling them he was "touring with my new band with Rob Fish opening for the guys from Youth of Today's new band."

years.h: Shows turn to brawls when the anti-Krishna flyers come out
years.p: Chris Daly told The Guardian that fights broke out at 108 shows between the band and people handing out flyers that compared Krishna consciousness to Nazi indoctrination.
years.xp: Daly made the point in 2026, looking back on his time in the band. No Echo has written up an anti-Krishna flyer incident in the scene as early as 1990, before 108 existed.

years.src: Discogs · No Echo: Chris Daly · The Vinyl Factory
years.h: Songs of Separation gets cut at Don Fury's New York studio
years.p: Kate Reddy plays guitar and sings and Chris Daly drums on 108's second Equal Vision album, with Vic DiCara on guitar and bass.
years.xp:
Daly learned the songs from a four-track cassette DiCara had recorded alone at the band's Philadelphia temple, with instructions to treat it as a template and play it how he felt. His reaction, he told No Echo: "I was completely blown away by the power and ferocity of all the new songs."

Reddy, credited as Kate 08, co-owned Equal Vision with her husband Steve Reddy. She also led Project Kate with [[Norman Brannon|fbe11657-2638-4486-8369-2157644a9031]] and Sergio Vega.

The Vinyl Factory suggests the album's title may be a nod to the Holyname pressing error that ran the songs together as one track.

years.src: The Guardian · No Echo: Chris Daly
years.h: Texas Is the Reason pulls Chris Daly away from 108
years.p: Daly starts the band with [[Norman Brannon|fbe11657-2638-4486-8369-2157644a9031]] after Songs of Separation; they bonded, he told The Guardian, over 10,000 Maniacs and Ride.

eras.title: The cameras come, then DiCara goes
eras.text: New bassists, a documentary crew and a hard European run kept 108 moving. By 1996 there was a third album on a German label and a last tour on film, and DiCara was headed for India.

years.h: Franklin Rhi takes the bass, then walks out after Europe
years.p: The [[Crown of Thornz|e7b3e015-81fa-4180-aa7b-7bfcf821209d]] bassist meets Vic DiCara at the Krishna temple and is handed the band's record to learn. After a 1995 European tour he quits both bands.
years.xp:
Rhi told No Echo that the outgoing bassist suggested him and it all felt seamless. Europe changed his head: "you're seeing some very serious poverty and hardship."

He left both 108 and Crown of Thornz: "I just had to just go away for a little bit." He later joined Shelter.

years.h: Frank Pavich's cameras catch 108 for N.Y.H.C.
years.p: The film pairs live 108 footage with interviews of Vic DiCara, Rob Fish and bassist Trivikrama Dasa. The soundtrack came out in 1996 to fund the film, which followed in 1999.

years.h: Threefold Misery has a drummer on loan from Atlantic Records
years.p: 108's third album comes out on Germany's Lost & Found, recorded at Salad Days Studio with Trivikrama Dasa on bass. The liner notes credit drummer Matt Cross as playing "courtesy of Atlantic Records."

years.src: Anti-Matter · Stuck in the Past · Wikipedia: 108 (band)
years.h: A last tour, on film, and then DiCara is gone to India
years.p: Evan Jacobs films 108's final US and European run. When it ends so does the band, and DiCara moves to India to live as a monk.
years.xp:
DiCara told Anti-Matter he went to Vrindavan and knew where he wanted to be: "I want to live here and die here." ISKCON leadership wanted him back preaching, and by 1996 or 1997 he was out of the institution: "I just said goodbye."

The film, Curse of Instinct, stayed out of print for years before it turned up on Google Video.

eras.title: The tape outlives the band
eras.text: The band was gone and the catalog wasn't. Lost & Found, Caroline and Reflections kept releases coming, and the final tour reached tape in 2000.

years.src: Wikipedia: 108 (band) · Discogs · Choose Your Heaven zine
years.h: The final-tour VHS arrives four years after the split
years.p: Curse of Instinct: 108's Final Tour and a live album of the same name appear in 2000, the album on Reflections Records.
years.xp:
The afterlife had started in 1997, with Lost & Found's Serve & Defy EP, the collection One Path for Me Through Destiny, and a 108 track on Caroline's Misfits tribute Violent World.

Rob Fish, meanwhile, had left ISKCON in 1997 after nine years; he later took initiation in the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition at Radha Kunda in India. He told Choose Your Heaven it was his discomfort with religious institutions that led him away from the group.

eras.title: Back, without the temple
eras.text: 108 came back in 2005 with Rob Fish and Vic DiCara both outside ISKCON. They signed to Deathwish Inc., made two records in the Converge circle, and in 2010 nearly lost their singer over what the band still meant.

years.h: Hellfest cancels, and 108's comeback moves to Philadelphia
years.p: 108 re-form in August 2005 with Trivikrama Dasa on bass and Tom Hogan on drums, aiming for Hellfest. Legal issues cancel the festival at the last moment, and the band re-books gigs in Philadelphia.
years.xp:
DiCara told Punknews his eight years inside the Hare Krishna institutions taught him "I have very low tolerance for organized religion." Fish said the spiritual inspiration was the same but "the external and social aspects have changed dramatically."

DiCara later told Anti-Matter the restart was "good and bad" because "it's like when you give a kid access to the candy store."

In 2006 Equal Vision collected the 1990s catalog on the two-disc Creation. Sustenance. Destruction., and the band self-released Oneoeight, a demo EP.

years.cap: Rob Fish at Max Destruction Fest, Essen, Germany
q: Emotionally, it is the heaviest record we have ever created.
years.src: Punknews · Discogs · Wikipedia: A New Beat from a Dead Heart
years.h: Kurt Ballou gets A New Beat from a Dead Heart done in about six days
years.p: 108's first album in eleven years comes out on Deathwish, recorded in February 2007 at [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]]'s GodCity studio in Salem, Massachusetts.
years.xp:
Discogs credits Tom Hogan on drums and both Trivikrama Dasa and Tim Cohen on bass. The band had signed to Deathwish, run by Converge's [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]], in January 2007.

DiCara told Punknews: "Kurt really bent over backwards and gave so much more than we paid him for."

years.h: Rob Fish quits in March and is back by September
years.p: Fish announces on March 23, 2010 that he is leaving, saying he can't find his place in the band after his personal evolution. By September he has rejoined.
years.xp: Lambgoat ran the news as a breakup. The band's own statement said "108 has not broken up", and Vic DiCara answered that 108 would carry on without a replacement and do something very different. It never came to that.

years.cap: Vic DiCara at Muggefug, Cottbus, Germany
yt: Rob Fish interview and live, 924 Gilman, 2009
years.h: Deathwish files 18.61 as DWI108
years.p: Named for chapter 18, verse 61 of the Bhagavad Gita, 108's fifth album has Mike Justian on drums, Tim Cohen on bass and Jacob Bannon guesting.
years.xp: It was recorded in Boston in February 2009 with producer Alex Garcia-Rivera and mixed by Kurt Ballou. Deathwish gave it the catalog number DWI108, a 108 for a band named 108.

eras.title: The old records get played in full
eras.text: Twenty years on, 108 started playing the old albums in full, with the people who made them. Kate Reddy came back first.

years.h: Twenty years on, Kate Reddy plays with 108 again
years.p: It happens on May 21 in Flemington, New Jersey. Cambridge's Middle East opens the run and Brooklyn's Saint Vitus closes it with two sets.
years.xp: Saint Vitus split the catalog: the 1 PM set drew on Holyname and Songs of Separation, and the 6 PM set on Threefold Misery, Curse of Instinct, A New Beat from a Dead Heart and 18.61. Blacklisted and Sweet Jesus opened both Brooklyn shows.

years.h: DiCara tells it himself in Train Wrecks & Transcendence
years.p: Subtitled A Collision of Hardcore & Hare Krishna, it covers his Inside Out, Shelter and 108 years. Deathwish reissues Threefold Misery on vinyl the same year.
years.xp: Norman Brannon's Anti-Matter later described DiCara as having left ISKCON after about a decade as a monk and working as a Vedic astrologer and Sanskrit translator in Japan.

years.cap: Vic DiCara at Brooklyn Bazaar, Brooklyn, November 2019
years.h: Songs of Separation turns 25 on blue vinyl, with exactly 108 copies
years.p: Two New York shows mark the anniversary, one at Brooklyn Bazaar. Equal Vision's remastered pressing is limited to 108 copies, sold only at the shows.
years.xp: BrooklynVegan's announcement put Brooklyn Bazaar on November 2 and said the venue for the November 1 show was still to come.

years.cap: Vic DiCara and Rob Fish at Brooklyn Monarch, Brooklyn, October 21, 2023
years.h: Judge and 108 co-headline Boston, Brooklyn and Hamden
years.p: Middle East in Boston on October 20, Brooklyn Monarch on the 21st, Space Ballroom in Hamden, Connecticut on the 22nd.
years.xp:
The Monarch night also had Age of Apocalypse, Wild Side and Roll Call on the bill.

In his Anti-Matter conversation DiCara said he no longer felt motivated to play in 108, and "being happy is not good for 108."
